emma_support: @eng-runtime heads up — Acme SaaS (tenant acme-tenant) reporting lots of 429s and high p95 on /v1/generate from dedicated pool eu-west-2 ded-7. Started ~09:12 UTC. They say workloads include very long contexts (~40-60k tokens).

emma_support: logs show repeated kv eviction pressure and allocation failures. Snippet:
```
[09:12:33] kv-cache: eviction_pressure level=critical tenant=acme-tenant used_pct=92 fragments=18
[09:12:33] runtime: alloc failed size=128MiB reason=insufficient_kv_mem tenant=acme-tenant
[09:12:34] throttle: 429 route=/v1/generate model=text-xl seq_len=52000 pool=ded-7
```

dylan_support: customer provided a repro curl that spikes within 2 minutes. sharing below.

emma_support: repro (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"text-xl","input":"<40k tokens ...>","max_tokens":1024}'
```

jason_runtime: thx. I'm seeing matching metrics from ded-7 — KV high-water mark, then large eviction waves. Paging eng-sre for autoscale and fragmentation checks. @priya_sre

priya_sre: on it. initial dashboard: ded-7 had a scale-in at 08:50, autoscaler backoff is still in effect (configured backoff=12m after last scale). That prevented adding capacity during the spike. Also node-level mem fragmentation high on GPUs 2/3 — likely due to repeated long-sequence allocations and freed KV slabs.

priya_sre: quick theory: long-context requests force large KV allocations, fragmentation prevents efficient reuse, KV cache eviction runs aggressively and then throttles new requests. Autoscaler didn't react because of cooldown/backoff.

emma_support: customer also reported increased latencies preceding 429s. They saw many small successful responses then a steep drop with bursts of 429.

jason_runtime: can we confirm whether prefix caching is enabled for this tenant? That can amplify KV usage for long contexts.

dylan_support: acme_oncall: can you confirm if you enabled prefix_kv_cache for your long-context pipeline last week?

acme_oncall: yes we turned on prefix_kv_cache for cost reasons 3 days ago. it reduced token costs but we started seeing errors after yesterday's heavy batch run.

priya_sre: OK that aligns. Action plan: 1) temporarily move acme-tenant to isolation pool (ded-13) to stop noisy neighbor impact 2) increase per-tenant kv_cache_limit on ded-13 3) disable prefix_kv_cache for long-context routes as emergency rollback 4) schedule immediate compaction job on ded-7 nodes and clear fragmented slabs 5) adjust autoscaler cooldown/backoff for pools with frequent long-context patterns.

jason_runtime: i can provision ded-13 slot and migrate traffic. initiating migration now. deploy-bot: start migration job for tenant=acme-tenant target_pool=ded-13

deploy-bot: started job 8921 — migrating routing for tenant=acme-tenant -> ded-13. estimated 90s.

priya_sre: while migration runs, i'm triggering a KV slab compaction on ded-7 to reclaim fragmented memory. Also bumping kv_cache_limit for acme on ded-13 to 48GiB.

priya_sre: compaction started. autoscaler config change queued: reduce backoff to 3m for pools tagged long-context=true. We will run this as a canary in eu-west-2 only.

emma_support: customer put a temporary mitigation in place: they reverted prefix caching earlier and are throttling their long-batch jobs. but they want platform fix.

acme_oncall: after migration started we saw 200s -> 2xx on new pool for a subset of requests. still some errors in the old pool during cutover.

jason_runtime: migration finished. routing now points to ded-13 for acme-tenant. monitoring p95 and 429 rate.

priya_sre: compaction finished. ded-7 memory fragmentation dropped from 72% -> 26% after compaction. evictions rate down 85%. autoscaler change deployed to canary.

dylan_support: customer confirms 429s dropped to baseline after migration and disabling prefix cache. They want root cause analysis and follow-ups: 1) better autoscale policy for long-context tenants, 2) fragmentation mitigation (periodic compaction), 3) telemetry to detect repeated large kv allocations.

jason_runtime: agreed. follow-ups: PR to autoscaler to add backoff override when pool contains tagged long-context tenants, add a KV fragmentation metric (kv_fragmentation_ratio) to per-pool dashboards, and implement an admin toggle to disable prefix_kv_cache per-route. I'll open tickets.

priya_sre: filing incident follow-up doc with timeline and remediation. recommend adding an alert: when eviction_pressure>60% and scale_possible=true, trigger immediate proactive scale.

emma_support: thanks team. customer happy for now but they asked for a post-mortem and plan before we close. I'll coordinate with Acme for a post-mortem session. :handshake:

dylan_support: notes for handoff: repro steps + sanitized logs + compaction job id + autoscaler PR link will be attached in the post-mortem.

priya_sre: final note: long-context workloads are increasingly common. we should treat KV fragmentation as a first-class SLO risk for dedicated pools.

emma_support: closing loop here when post-mortem doc is ready. thanks. :white_check_mark:
